tasks.task: Turn rough notes into a clear recipe card

items.when: When a recipe is new or keeps failing for others, to run draft, test and fix in order
When the cook's notes are a voice memo, to turn it into text first
When you have rough notes, an old card or a transcript and need a card anyone can follow
When you need yield, times, pan size, ingredients in order of use and doneness cues
When one step hides a technique, to break it into small steps with the usual mistake
When the method assumes skill, to ask what a nervous home baker needs to be told
When the card is drafted, to swap chef words for plain ones

tasks.task: Scale a recipe or convert its units

items.when: When you need a recipe at a new yield, batch size or pan size
When every amount must be multiplied, converted and rounded to amounts a cook can measure
When a big batch behaves differently, to ask what physical change does not scale in a line
After scaling, to check every unit and how rounding errors add up
When the batch is for a catered event, to check the order against the quote and guest needs

tasks.task: Write standard recipe cards for a kitchen team

items.when: When a restaurant, cafe or caterer needs every cook to make a dish the same way
When the dish needs one page of standards a cook can check: weight, colour, time, plating
When prep spans stations, to write who does what and in what order
When new cooks must learn the dish, to make a one-page handout for the pass
When the card lists steps but not the technique that makes them work
When the card is dense, to find where a new cook would be overloaded
When a recipe must work for someone other than its author: criteria, test sheet and testers
When one thing is in doubt, to set a clear question and change only that
When choosing testers, to pick an expert and a beginner and what to ask each
When several versions need tasting side by side, to plan the session and the taster card
When tests wander, to set a target, change one thing and measure it

tasks.task: Find why a recipe keeps failing for other cooks

items.when: When reader or staff reports say the recipe does not work, to retest it in order
When you need a test sheet for weights, times and temperatures to find the fault
When the dish is bland or flat, to check salt, fat, acid and heat in turn
When a step fails for no clear reason, to ask what is happening to the food itself
When you think you know the cause, to confirm it with one controlled test

tasks.task: Write a recipe blog post around a tested recipe

items.when: Before writing, to find the questions readers ask and how they search for them
When the recipe is tested and you want a post that helps readers make it, with no padding
When the post needs a headnote, disclosure, the card, tips, swaps and reader questions
When the title is plain, to compare several honest angles
When the headnote is filler, to say why this recipe earns a place in a real week
When the post is drafted, to match each claim to proof and make the words plain
Before publishing, to fix lines that read as machine written

tasks.task: Publish recipes online with markup and search basics

items.when: When tested recipes are ready for the site, or old recipe posts need fixing
Before publishing a batch, to rank the searches worth a post
When each recipe page needs markup for rich results, tested and ready to paste
When the page needs a search title, description and share tags that fit
When the page is live, to get fixes for headings, links and content

tasks.task: Fix or refresh old recipe posts

items.when: When old posts lack a proper card, markup or tested amounts
When many posts are fading, to decide refresh, merge or cut for each and track it
When you have the list, to see how deep each update should go

tasks.task: Plan recipe content from what readers ask

items.when: When the blog covers everything, to find the few subjects the cook can own
When you have a topic, to group searches by what the reader wants
When you have comments and emails, to turn reader questions into post ideas
When a bakery or food shop sells online and posts should lift its product pages

tasks.task: Write a cookbook proposal or chapter plan

items.when: Before the proposal, to stress-test the book idea and cut it to one page
When you want to pitch a cookbook to an agent or publisher, or plan one to self-publish
When the author needs an outline and a writing plan for their stage
When a chapter's recipes and essays need a clear order
When the book needs a title, to compare several angles

tasks.task: Prepare a nutrition and allergen data pack

items.when: When a recipe is moving into a packaged product and a qualified person will work out the label
When the product needs shelf life, safe handling and tracing planned
When weights per serving are worked out, to check units and rounding
When you have ingredient prices, to get cost per portion and contribution for one batch
When real yield differs from the recipe, to turn measured yield into cost per good unit
When trim and cooking loss are large, to find the true cost per good kilogram
When costing needs the recipe at the batch size the kitchen really makes

tasks.task: Brief the photos and step shots for a recipe

items.when: When photos are planned, to list each shot and the reason for it
When the post needs a cover image that fits the piece
Before scripting, to pick a format and get a script outline
When one long cook-along should become a plan of shorter videos
When clips are shot, to get a timed cut list, captions and a cover
When the opening is drafted, to score it and get rewrites

tasks.task: Write social posts and a newsletter from recipes

items.when: When posts are ad hoc, to set a rolling calendar with captions
When one recipe needs clear posts for each platform
When a recipe newsletter runs every week and should match past issues
Before sending, to compare subject lines from several angles
When the issue is drafted, to get cuts and a ship or fix call

tasks.task: Write dish names and menu descriptions

items.when: When a description is vague, to make it short, true and easy to picture
When the menu says local, homemade or free-from, to check each claim can be backed

tasks.task: Adapt a recipe for a diet, allergy or another country

items.when: When the new market uses other units, pan sizes or oven settings
When the card must read naturally in another language with local ingredient names
When an ingredient is swapped, to keep the balance of salt, fat, acid and heat
After any swap, to retest before the adapted card is shared

tasks.task: Edit a set of recipes to one style

items.when: When the blog or kitchen has no written style, to set one before editing
When old cards must follow one order, one set of units and one way of naming things
When the set is long, to list term clashes and slips without rewriting
Last pass on the set, with a log of every change

tasks.task: Package recipes as an ebook or free guide

items.when: When the cook wants a free guide that leads readers to what they sell next
When the ebook needs a chapter plan and a recipe list
When the ebook is for sale and needs a price and launch emails

always.when: Whenever an amount, unit or temperature changes, to check the sums before the card goes out
When a post makes a health, nutrition or origin claim, to check it against a trusted source
Before delivery, to catch stock phrases that make a post read as machine written
Last step before sign-off, to catch slips in amounts, times and names

helpers.when: When the recipe needs finished photos, step shots or image edits
When standard recipes feed menu pricing, ordering and kitchen training
When the recipe site needs a search audit or a keyword plan beyond one post
When the cookbook needs chapters and essays written in the cook's voice
When a packaged food needs label rules checked for the country it sells in
When recipe posts need scheduling, replies and a channel plan

gaps: No library item writes, scales or converts recipes; cards, baker's percentages and pan-size changes rest on the kit alone
No library item works out nutrition values or builds an allergen table, and none knows food label rules by country
No library item suggests ingredient swaps for a diet or allergy and says what else must change
No library item gives a recipe test sheet or scores a tasting panel; general test planners stand in
No library item checks recipe markup for search; the markup writers are general
No library item plans food photos or styling; a product shot list stands in
No library item scripts a hands-and-pans recipe video
No library item writes a cookbook proposal with comparable titles and a sample chapter
No library item writes menu descriptions or makes different versions to compare
No library item gives safe cooling, storing and reheating notes to put on a card
